Unified? One mechanism and one scaling explain where the effect appears and how big it is. It is measured only in strip µTPCs.

Paper? Yes, as a measurement with a survey: per-track reference, decomposition, coupling bound, remedies on the same tracks.

1

Details

Question 1: did we understand the effect in a unified way in all TPCs? As one mechanism and one scaling, yes. As a test, only for strip µTPCs. Pad TPCs and LArTPCs are explained by a long column and so predicted to show nothing, directional detectors have no reference, GridPix has nothing to aggregate. One published result does not fit (Scholer's test beam, slide 8).

Question 2: can we add to the literature? Yes. The new content is the per-track measurement, the decomposition, the depth and position-in-strip tests of the coupling, and the remedies scored on the same tracks.

2

Details

Displacing the two ends of a least-squares line through N strips rotates it by an amount that falls as 1/N². So ratio − 1 = tan_rec/tan_true − 1 ≈ C/N² + b, with N = L tanθ/p the strips in the drift column. C holds the end displacements; b is any interior compression.

The published "capacitive coupling" is one way of feeding the ghost strips. Diffusion, the induction footprint and resistive spreading feed them too.

Hover the data points and dotted terms for values. Details hold the method and caveats. Draft: papers/tpc_mixing_review/main.pdf.

4

Details

The two-parameter fit of Δtan = a/tan + b·tan gives C = a(L/p)². χ²/ndf: X Run 1 51/9, Y Run 1 5/8, X Run 2 114/9, Y Run 2 7/9. So on X the form is a good description but not a statistically complete one. The paper must state this; quoting C alone hides it. Above N ≈ 9 the quantity is a small difference, so any 1 % angle-scale error moves (ratio − 1)N² strongly.

The data ratios use the calibrated angle scale (w_ref = kw·v·tan + w0). The timing velocity inflates every ratio by kw − 1 and looks like an interior term.

5

Details

This replaces the "share of coupling vs footprint", which is a parametrisation of one variance and has no meaning. Moving charge between a Gaussian footprint and a nearest-neighbour coupling of equal variance leaves the compression unchanged.

The arms carry the real data residual, so they include whatever the model does not describe. The clean white-noise toy gives the same increments about one unit lower (C = 6.0 for the full X model, against the data's 7.0). "Reproduced to 2 %" therefore means the arms-with-residual; the pure model is about 15 % below on X.

Draft correction: the text quotes RC as +4.6, which is model Y − model X (11.5 − 6.9). Switching RC off on Y gives +4.2.

6

Details

C is the leading-edge end coefficient; σ_rms is the lateral spread averaged over the column. The constant is the strip geometry and the quadratic term the ghost strips. The orange points use a different shaper (50 ns CR–RC², 25 ns sampling, Fermi-Dirac time) and fall on the same line; that is a real check, since they were not in the fit. Other estimators move C by about ±20 %.

Chamber A data at k = 1 sits about one unit above the line, which the draft traces to the unmodelled same-time floor (slide 12). The line is dominated at the top by one point, p = 0.39 mm.

The law holds for X-type spreading only. The RC term on Y is not in it.

7

Details

Measured points quote a most probable or mean angle of a selected distribution, against a set angle known to about 1° (Bortfeldt gives 10 ± 1°). At 10° that is about 10 % in tan, as large as the effect.

Not in the draft's figure. Scholer 2021 (NSW, VMM): the test-beam peak equals the true 28°, while the simulation with sharing off peaks 7° high. Klitzner's MSc reports most layers slightly small in Ne:CF4. Ntekas's gas-only simulation (0.2° at 30°) and Scholer's sharing-off simulation (7° above 25°) differ by more than an order of magnitude, and neither source explains why. The ±1° bars are illustrative, not each paper's own error.

Sources: hits_daq/literature_survey/strip_microtpcs.md, hits_daq/reports/Capacitive coupling in strip microTPCs.md.

8

Details

The toy uses D_T = 365 µm/√cm for all, a footprint of 0.10 mm (0.15 for the GEM), a 50 ns CR–RC² shaper sampled at 25 ns, and the Fermi-Dirac rise time of the LMU analyses. The VMM points use the peak time.

Agreement to a factor 1.7 on ratio − 1, with four points and an assumed diffusion, is a consistency check. The draft's phrase "within the uncertainty of their assumed footprints" should say this number.

Against the simulations the toy is less close: Ntekas's gas-only value at 30° is 1.008 where the toy gives 1.105. The circuit model of Bortfeldt, which has coupling but no diffusion, also lands near these values: the angle alone cannot tell the two apart. Scholer's test beam is the one measured result the picture misses; its 7.1° resolution, peak-based statistic and angle cuts may explain it, but nobody has shown that.

9

Details

Pad TPCs and LArTPCs have the same spread in pitch units as MX17, but columns 10–100 times longer. They also read a charge-weighted or deconvolved time. Their drift scale is fixed to 0.1 % by lasers and silicon, so no compression is expected or seen.

The contours extrapolate the toy law to N and σ/p outside its fit (fit range N ≲ 20, σ_rms/p ≲ 1.3) and to estimators it was not fit to. Read them as order-of-magnitude. Values come from the draft's Table 1 and are derived from published geometry; the LMU diffusion is assumed.

The GridPix point is at N = 110, where the law would apply only if many electrons shared a time; each electron has its own, so nothing is aggregated.

Unified as one mechanism; tested only where the column is short

FamilyEvidenceStatus
Strip µTPC, MX17Per-track reference, 4 chambers, full decompositionTested

Pad TPC (ALICE, STAR, T2K)Column 10–100× longer, charge-weighted time; bias < 0.1 % predictedExplained, untested
LArTPCHundreds of wires, 2-D deconvolution; short segments never testedExplained, untested
Directional, short trackHas the column; describes end artefacts, but no reference to reveal a slope biasCannot be tested
GridPixOne time per electronEffect absent by design
Drift tubesAngle-dependent space-time relation: same idea, already calibrated inAnalogy only

So: a single account of why the effect appears, in which detectors, and how big. Not a measurement in every TPC, and the dataset cannot make it one.

10

Details

"Unified" is justified in this sense: the formula needs only N and σ/p, and the absence of the effect in long-column detectors follows from it. The paper should not claim that the long-column and directional families have been shown to obey it.

11

Details

Plotted to 800 ns: beyond the column end the share is a ratio of tails and diverges on Y. The first-neighbour share is (W₋₁ + W₊₁)/W₀ in the same drift-time slice. Without diffusion the model stays flat. The rate of growth prefers D_p ≈ 0.021 mm/√ns (D_T ≈ 350 µm/√cm), 8 % below the pass value, a recorded tension in docs/PARAMETERS.md.

On Y the resistive spreading adds most of the growth. The mesh-end value says a same-time share is required: the metallic arm starts at half the data's value.

At depth the second-neighbour share exceeds every arm, so the lateral tails are heavier than Gaussian. Its origin is not identified.

A fixed coupling is bounded at about 6 % (X) and 10 % (Y) per neighbour

A Gaussian footprint falls off across the strip; a fixed coupling stays flat. Published coupling values are 15–30 %.

12

Details

The closure curves are windows regenerated with known truth and fresh white noise, then refitted with the production fitter exactly like the data. Refit minus truth is 0.007 mm (Gaussian) to 0.07 mm (coupling), so the test is not an artefact of the fitted position.

X: far share flat at 0.060–0.067 from a quarter pitch out, between Gaussian (0.040) and 13 % coupling (0.127). Y: 0.10 at the edge, with the centre bin below the Gaussian: the Y core is narrower than the fitted 0.28 mm.

Draft inconsistency: the first paragraph of sec. 5.4 says no same-time floor is required on Y; the closure paragraph finds one at 0.10. The closure paragraph is the one that stands. The bound is on this chamber only.

13

Details

The truth here is the fit's own slope on the calibrated scale, not the silicon reference, on the clean bootstrap planes. Absolute C on chamber A is 10–15 % lower than on the full sample (7.0/11.6), so only chamber-to-chamber comparison means anything.

Chamber E's X value is the outlier against the toy law (8.0 against 5.8); it has dead and low-gain bands and a short column. Chamber D's X has 177 planes and Y too few to fit. Chamber C is excluded (92 % saturated).

Draft correction: the conclusions say the three further chambers reproduce the model within 10 % on both views. Chamber D's X does not (7.2 against 5.1, 177 planes).

14

Details

Edge cut and shift lower the raw bias by 10–15 % at every angle on X (the toy predicts 24 %). Draft correction: the section heading and the conclusions say "a quarter". The 15 % subtraction reduces the resolution gap to the waveform fit by about 40 %; the text says "halves".

30 % subtraction helps X and hurts Y, where the neighbours' signals are real delayed RC charge. The charge-weighted time alone does nothing, since there is no interior term to remove. The forward model on hit lists is close to the waveform fit: most of the remaining gap is information that hits do not keep.

16

Details

A review journal would expect balanced coverage; this has one new dataset at its centre and takes a position. NIM A or JINST fit it. The venue and author list are Dylan's decision (\tbw marks in the draft).

Overlap: the forward fit and H2c should stay in Paper II and be cited. The draft leans on Papers I and II, so its submission order matters. The novelty rows are stated as "not found" because the search was limited: Alexopoulos 2019 (NIM A 937) is closed-access and unread, and internal ATLAS/BESIII notes are not public.

Details

The draft-vs-table discrepancies are from reading sections 5, 6 and 8 against tables 2–5 and the result files; the corrected numbers are computed on the matching slides. "Effort" is my estimate.

The DAGs were not scored for this deck. See the handoff for the scoring steps.

What this does not rule out, and what is yours to decide

Not ruled out

  • Real coupling of 15–30 % in the other chambers: the bound is on chamber A.
  • A different cause of Scholer's unshifted test beam, or a limit of the picture on VMM chambers.
  • A same-time process we have not named: the 6–10 % floor has no origin.
  • Short segments in long-drift TPCs: predicted a few per cent, never measured.
  • Everything measured here is one gas, one drift field, 60 ns DREAM sampling.

Your decisions

  • Keep it as a third paper, and call it a measurement rather than a review.
  • Whether Paper II keeps its own sections 3 and 6 or points here.
  • Authors and venue.
  • Is chamber C worth a window extraction, given 92 % saturation?
